subject.title: [Feature]: Automatic Output Sanitization for Sensitive Data

question: Should OpenClaw own automatic sensitive-value sanitization for final visible agent output in core, or should this be an optional plugin/ClawHub capability built on outbound hooks?
rationale: Source inspection proves the gap, but the behavior changes a security boundary, user-visible output, and possibly config defaults; automation cannot choose the acceptable false-positive policy or core-versus-plugin ownership.

options.title: Approve a narrow core sanitizer
options.body: Define an opt-in or carefully scoped core policy that reuses existing redaction helpers and includes schema, docs, delivery-path tests, and false-positive coverage.

options.title: Route to plugin or ClawHub
options.body: Keep core limited to hooks and existing redaction boundaries, and ask for a sanitizer plugin package with manifest metadata, permissions/config, docs, and smoke proof.

options.title: Declare existing boundaries sufficient
options.body: Close or narrow the request if maintainers want core to redact only logs, transcripts, tool/UI diagnostics, and internal scaffolding rather than final replies.

recommendation.title: Approve a narrow core sanitizer
recommendation.body: Define an opt-in or carefully scoped core policy that reuses existing redaction helpers and includes schema, docs, delivery-path tests, and false-positive coverage.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision is a security boundary and config-default choice, and CODEOWNERS routes security-sensitive config/secrets/docs to this owner group.
